review_kind: Independent, read-only Claude re-review (attempt 03) of Academy 2.1 milestone 1 (qualification tooling and fixtures). Not hosted acceptance, not release approval, and not the formal independent Codex chunk/phase gate. The hosted archive was read only to check what the doc and summary claim.
required_fixes: RF1 The redaction claim is still false for one receipt type: authored answers, `values` and membership/equality literals are written verbatim to the device sign-in receipt. receipt_input redacts `/json/answer` and `/json/values` only in per-call receipts (assertions.rs:268-281). The sign-in receipt is settled with `ctx.run.inputs(sign_in_family, &[])` (live_academy.rs:398-404), and Run::inputs copies every nonsecret manifest entry, including the raw `call.*` strings (live_run.rs:1053-1064). When L11 is not selected, sign_in_family is the lead program family (live_academy.rs:397). That is the hosted configuration. The archive shows the leak: hosted/receipts/b4c3…/L12/L11-device-sign-in.json `inputs.call.02-inline` contains `"answer":999999`, and receipts/23dc…/L12/L11-device-sign-in.json contains the membership literal `["mcq","scenario","config-diagnosis"]` verbatim. The value there is a deliberately wrong index, so nothing sensitive leaked. But a `/correct=true` inline answer or a Shift `values` list would publish an answer key into committed receipts. That contradicts follow-up.md:55-57 ('redacts `answer` and `values` fields … Membership literals are summarized too'). Fix: leave `call.*` out of the sign-in/admission receipt inputs, or pass each one through the same template redaction and summarize its expectation literals. Then add a fixture assertion (assert_no_secret on a distinctive authored answer and `values` element, e.g. in the L12-only daily_program run) that covers every receipt file, not only the per-call receipt.
evidence_gaps: G1 (prior) closed. The authorized `python3 -B docs/planning/reviews/academy-2.1/attempt-03/audit.py` printed {"read_only_audit":"passed","validation_records":3,"bound_build_inputs":178,"hosted_receipt_hashes":13}. For each of the last three run.json records it confirmed exit 0 and build_inputs_unchanged. It also confirmed the log sha256, all 178 build-input hashes against the current files (these include the four scoped Rust files, live_run.rs, desktop-core learner.rs, Cargo.lock, case-catalog.json, scm-catalog.json and resources/harness/pin.json), the live_run and xtask test-executable hashes, the attempt-03 inputs.json hashes and all 13 hosted receipt hashes. The logs read 49/49 live_run tests, 21/21 unit tests, and clippy `-D warnings` finished cleanly. The audit binds recorded hashes to the current files. It does not show that the executables were compiled from those inputs; that rests on the recorded build_inputs_unchanged flag.
G2 (prior) closed for all three records. The compile-time JSON assets and pin.json are now in build_inputs. The clippy record still has no executable hash, which is acceptable for a lint run.

G3 The hosted receipts come from three earlier runner/source fingerprints (runner 79134985…, 76c0193f…, 51373d65…). None is the final validated build. They show what the core and Academy did at the time, not the behavior of the reviewed source. hosted/inline-run.json is not in summary.receipts, so the audit does not hash-bind it.

G4 The hosted archive supports the summary's claims, and only those. Sign-in passed, and the core-observed account_sha256 ac717998… matches expected_account_sha256 in both pinned manifests (b4c3, 23dc). The f295 catalog-read sign-in, which ran before the hash was pinned, observed the same hash. courses.list returned an array_len of 50 (f295). The 8c1e catalog attempt was honestly recorded as blocked by budget. Course summary: hasProgress=false, all four counts 0. Inline grading used lessonId and questionId references taken from units.get, and returned correct=false. certificate.mine=[], exam.eligibility eligible=false, shift.eligibility unlocked=false with poolCount 0 of minQuestions 50. These are disclosed test-data prerequisites, not implementation defects. W53, W65, W66 and certificate preservation are not qualified. The summary itself says 'partial; no W53/W65/W66 completion'. follow-up.md:144-148 still describes only sign-in plus the catalog read. It does not mention the correct=false inline grading or the three prerequisite blockers that summary.json records.

G5 The pure contract tests remove every mandatory expectation individually (contracts.rs:374-391), and that claim holds. Not every input-identity binding is exercised on its own: exam.submissionState's `/json/attemptId` input reference (only the Same assertion is removed), shift.answer's `/json/order` reference to the last serve (the test replaces the whole input, so the shiftId check fails first), shift.start's `daily:true` (the loop starts at index 1), and the resetCourse call's own courseId (only the `after` call's courseId is altered, contracts.rs:422-424). The code does enforce each of these (contracts.rs:109, 117, 158, 183). Only the regression coverage is missing.

G6 Carried hosted-planning gaps, not milestone-1 defects. Nothing yet shows how a deterministic Shift miss is produced so that `/themes:nonempty-array` can pass. The out-of-range inline answer 999999 was graded false, which suggests but does not prove the approach works for Shift. resetCourse deletes course-scoped exam attempts, so a W53 attempt and a W66 reset on the same course in one L13 run would collide. `irreversible_exclusions` is still not enforced.
optional_suggestions: S1 Hand-off cleanup can still be skipped without a reconciliation record. If the calls budget runs out after shift.start (live_academy.rs:563-567), or the start answer arrives but fails its assertions so the decide input cannot resolve (live_academy.rs:546-560), the runner stops or blocks, and the spent Daily run gets no needs-reconciliation receipt. Academy makes the second case unlikely: a new start always returns alertsAnswered 0 and atBoundary false, and an existing run is CONFLICT (shift-run.ts:1969-1974). Consider refusing, before dispatch, a W65 program whose call count exceeds the remaining budget. Also consider marking any W65 run that stops after a successful start as needs-reconciliation.

S2 Consider requiring the answer immediately before shift.decide to assert `/next="boundary"`. The real AnswerResult has `next` (shift-run.ts:256). A known mid-stage hand-off would then be blocked instead of sent and refused with BAD_REQUEST. The Daily attempt is spent either way, but the receipt would be clearer.

S3 Hard-refuse irreversible learner mutations that this qualification must never send, whatever permitted_operations says: exam.submit, exam.answer, exam.acknowledgeAward, enrollment.removeByCourse, shop.buy, identityPractical.claimCertificate. Alternatively, enforce `irreversible_exclusions`. Today an operator-authored manifest is the only barrier (live_academy.rs:264-273).

S4 Multi-tag calls such as `W54,W66 progress.resetCourse` pass, because the W66 contract still applies, and they also earn W54 credit. Consider restricting contract-governed procedures to exactly their workflow.
S5 Redact by allowlist rather than two fixed pointers (assertions.rs:275). Other answer-bearing inputs, such as knowledge-check `answers` or exam answers, would then be covered by default.

S6 The template's L12/L13 reason text gives the grammar without ` ?? <expectation>` and does not mention `observe` or the procedure→workflow binding (live-manifest.template.json:227, 243). A one-line pointer would prevent surprises at authoring time. The `call.01-label: ""` placeholders fail closed.
S7 Carried: replace Box::leak ids and workflows with owned/Cow values (live_academy.rs:290, 366-368, 636).
limitations: Read-only review. The only command run was the authorized audit.py, plus file reads and greps. No builds, tests, clippy runs, endpoint calls or credential access. The private manifests themselves were not read. Their content is inferred from the inputs echoed in the hosted receipts.

Prior RF1 is confirmed resolved. contracts::validate first binds resetCourse→W66, exam.start→W53 and shift.start/serve/answer/decide→W65, independent of tags (contracts.rs:39-52). L12 cannot claim W53 or W66 (live_academy.rs:50-56), so a reset or exam start is impossible there. Duplicate limits cover exam.start/submissionState, shift.start/decide/debrief, resetCourse, and courseSummary/certificate.mine at most 2 (contracts.rs:61-81). Together with ordered matching, these limits mean the checked occurrence is the only occurrence. Every shift.serve and shift.answer is validated (contracts.rs:125-174), and each answer must reference the latest serve. The seven bypass routes are exercised unsent (academy.rs:973-1031).

Prior RF2 is confirmed resolved. The fixture refuses decide unless stage==3 with 400 'stage is not complete' (academy.rs:253-276), matching shift-run.ts:3106-3110. ungraded/breached no longer advance to a boundary (academy.rs:246-251). A failed or unconfirmed hand-off is recorded as needs-reconciliation with a stale-sweep note and stops with reconcile=true (live_academy.rs:603-614; live_run.rs:510-516; asserted at academy.rs:856-861). follow-up.md:47-49 lists ` ?? `, ` && ` and ` in `. Lines 80-84 state the boundary limit, and 90-96 bring the regression list up to date.

These follow-ups are also confirmed. The checkpoint receipt fails if any call in the same workflow failed (live_academy.rs:627). Membership literals are summarized (assertions.rs:168-171). dailyGhost and yesterday are exempt from the shiftId reference (contracts.rs:130-141). The fixture checks the checkInline lessonId/questionId and the courseSummary/resetCourse courseId (academy.rs:190-216). The wrong-exam-identity test now also asserts the sent attemptId (academy.rs:782-788), which answers prior G5.

Academy behavior was checked against the current local source (/Users/cdot/development/redtail/ai-security-academy/src/server: shift-run.ts startShift and decideStage, AnswerResult). The deployed service may differ.

The unsalted account_sha256 in receipts is acceptable only because Academy account IDs have high entropy. Concurrent C26/UI changes outside scope were not reviewed. Other places that might serialize manifest nonsecret values, such as ledger or run records, were not audited beyond the receipts named above.
recommendation: Minor revise, then proceed to the formal Codex gate. Both prior required fixes are actually fixed: contracts attach to procedures rather than tags, relabeling and duplicates are rejected before anything is sent, and hand-off cleanup matches real Academy semantics, with honest reconciliation. Prior G1 is closed by the passing hash audit. One real implementation defect remains. The device sign-in receipt copies raw `call.*` manifest entries, so authored answers, `values` and membership literals bypass the documented redaction (RF1). The hosted archive already shows this, harmlessly. It is a small, contained fix with a regression. The hosted exam, Shift, certificate-preservation and reset qualification are blocked by disclosed test-data prerequisites (no certificates, exam ineligible, Shift pool 0 of 50). They are correctly not claimed and do not count against this milestone-1 implementation verdict.
